title: Bolt Bumps Into Everything
learningObjectives: Explain that a robot senses, thinks and acts
Name the main parts of a robot
Describe how a distance sensor and a stop rule help a robot avoid obstacles

publishing.audienceNote: Children under 13; kid-appropriate tone, no external links.

scenes.title: Cold open: Bolt bumps into everything
scenes.educationalObjective: Hook: robots need to notice the world around them

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Ow! Who put a wall there?

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Bolt, that's not a wall. It's a pile of boxes. It's been there since Tuesday!

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Tuesday? That's sneaky! Boxes should beep before they jump out at people.

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Boxes don't beep, silly. Robots have to notice things by themselves. Today, you're going to learn how!

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Ooh! Is it a dance?

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Even better. It's Robotics 101!

scenes.title: Am I even a robot?
scenes.educationalObjective: A robot is a machine that can sense, think and act; examples of robots

concepts.title: What is a robot?
concepts.subtitle: It can sense, think and act

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Wait a second. Maya... am I even a real robot?

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Let's find out! A robot is a machine that can sense the world, think about what it senses, and then act.

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Sense, think, act. Got it! So my cousin the toaster is a robot!

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: The toaster doesn't think. It just makes toast. Sometimes very crispy toast.

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: But look, here's your real robot family!

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: A robot vacuum senses dirt and cleans the floor. A factory arm builds things, piece by piece.

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: And a space rover explores far-away places, all by itself!

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Wow. I come from a very hard-working family.

scenes.title: Robot check-up
scenes.educationalObjective: The five main parts of a robot: structure, sensors, actuators, power, controller

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Time for your robot check-up! Every robot has five main parts.

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: First, the structure. That's your body, the frame that holds everything together.

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Check out these structures!

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Next, sensors. They help you notice the world, a bit like eyes and ears.

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Actuators are the parts that move, like your wheels and your arms.

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Wheee!

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: The power source gives you energy. Hmm... your battery is a little low.

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: I'm not sleepy... you're sleepy...

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: And last, the controller. It's your robot brain, and it decides what to do.

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: My brain is fully charged and ready to think!

scenes.title: Sensors: ping!
scenes.educationalObjective: A distance sensor sends a sound and times the echo; it has a range

concepts.title: Distance sensors
concepts.subtitle: Ping! How far away is it?

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Let's test your distance sensor. It sends out a sound that's too high for people to hear.

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: The sound bounces off things and comes back. The faster the echo comes back, the closer the thing is. Bats do this too!

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: So I'm basically a bat. A bat with wheels!

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Nib, fly over there, please!

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Ping! Nib is 1.2 meters away!

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Perfect! Your sensor can measure things up to 3 meters away.

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Nib? Nib! My sensor can't find you!

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: He flew farther than 3 meters, so he's out of range.

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Phew. Don't scare me like that, buddy!

scenes.title: The stop-and-turn rule
scenes.educationalObjective: Sense, think, act: a controller rule with a 0.5 m threshold

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Now your robot brain needs a rule. Here's a good one.

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: If the distance is less than half a meter, stop and turn.

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Less than half a meter, stop and turn. Got it!

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Here's how it works. First you sense: your sensor measures the distance. Then you think: you compare it with the rule. Then you act: you keep going, or you stop and turn.

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Sense, think, act. Like a tiny dance, but with math!

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Let's practice. Sense!

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: 1.5 meters. Keep going!

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: 1 meter. Still fine!

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: 0.6 meters. Getting close...

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Is 0.6 less than 0.5?

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Nope! Bigger. So I keep going... slowly.

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: 0.4 meters! That's less than half a meter. STOP!

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Great stop! A little dramatic, but great.

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Sense, think, act. My antenna is glowing with brain power!

scenes.title: Actuators: high-five!
scenes.educationalObjective: Actuators turn decisions into movement; a servo turns to an exact angle

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Actuators turn decisions into movement. Your arm has a servo motor that turns to an exact angle.

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Let's try a high-five at 60 degrees!

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Sixty degrees? Easy peasy. Watch this!

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Oops! That was only 30 degrees.

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: The servo turns exactly as far as your brain tells it. Try sixty!

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: 60 degrees! High-five!

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: And a high-one for Nib!

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Motors turn wheels, servos turn arms, and I turn into a high-five champion!

scenes.title: The rematch
scenes.educationalObjective: Applying sense-think-act: stop and turn before the obstacle, then keep going

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Okay, Bolt. Time for a rematch with the boxes!

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Sense, think, act. Let's roll!

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Keep sensing the whole time. The boxes won't move, but you will!

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Sensing... sensing... boxes getting closer... still more than half a meter...

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Less than half a meter. Stop, and turn!

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Turning... and the path is clear! Rolling on!

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: You did it! No bonk!

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Victory spin!

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Remember, your sensor only sees what's in front of you!

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Noted.

scenes.title: Recap and quiz
scenes.educationalObjective: Recap sense-think-act and ask a question

parameters.question: Which part of a robot measures distance?

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Sense!

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Think!

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Act!

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Robots sense the world, think with a rule, and act with motors. Just like you did today, Bolt!

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: And I only bonked into one door. Well... two doors.

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Here's your question. Which part of a robot measures distance?

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: Think about it, and say your answer out loud!

beats.speaker: bolt
beats.text: Nib already knows. Show-off!

beats.speaker: maya
beats.text: See you next time on Robotics 101!
